t: All The Right Angles, a story about Ideal Box Co. on The Distance
s: Today, Ideal has reinvented itself to enable a more benign kind of vice: impulse buys at the grocery store. Its brightly colored bins and shelves, beckoning from the ends of aisles in supermarkets and big-box stores, might be just part of the scenery for shoppers, but they represent big business for the brands that pay to place them there—and for Scott and Yale Eisen, who run the corrugated box company that their great-grandfather started in 1924.
